clue.text: You fake broadcast? I'm not sure this can be played

indicators.note: something broadcast is heard rather than read, so these words are taken for their sound

parts.note: 'you' can be written U in text speak; a fake is PHONEY
UM is the noise of someone hesitating, unsure

explanation.surface: Someone doubts a radio programme was genuine and wonders whether an instrument can be played.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broadcast' turns 'U PHONEY' into the spoken start of the answer, spelt EUPHONI; then the hesitant UM finishes it.
explanation.definitionFit: A euphonium is a brass instrument, so it is something that can be played.

clue.text: The spirit of Dixieland

indicators.note: 'of' here means 'part of', so the letters are taken from inside the next word

explanation.surface: A nod to the lively character of Dixieland jazz.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer sits in the middle of DixiELANd.
explanation.definitionFit: Elan is dash and vigour, the spirit someone shows in doing something.

clue.text: Support pawns capturing rook, oddly

indicators.note: a piece that captures another takes it into itself, so one set of letters goes inside the other

parts.note: P is the chess abbreviation for pawn, so two pawns are PP

indicators.note: 'oddly' picks the odd-numbered letters of the word rook, its first and third

explanation.surface: A chess position where pawns back each other up while taking a rook.
explanation.definitionFit: A prop is something that holds something else up, a support.

clue.text: Ducks circling river come down in resort

indicators.note: two things circling something else surround it, so they go round the other letters

parts.note: a duck is a zero score in cricket, the letter O, so ducks are OO
to land is to come down to the ground

explanation.surface: Waterfowl wheel round a river before landing at a holiday spot.
explanation.walkthrough: The two Os go one at each end, round R and LAND. Orlando, Florida, is the resort, home to its theme parks.
explanation.definitionFit: Orlando in Florida is a famous holiday destination, a resort town.

clue.text: International legislation keeps any number relative

indicators.note: something that keeps another holds it inside, so one letter goes within the others

parts.note: law is legislation in general
N stands for an unspecified number in mathematics

explanation.surface: Global laws hold any number of relatives in their grip.
explanation.definitionFit: An in-law is someone related by marriage, a kind of relative.

clue.text: Look sharp as terrible cheats caught out underpinning manufacture

indicators.note: in a down answer a piece that underpins another sits below it, so it comes second

parts.note: to make is to manufacture

indicators.note: something done terribly is botched, so the remaining letters are jumbled
'out' means the letter for caught is left out of the word cheats

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: An urgent warning that some awful cheats have been caught out in a factory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' removes C from CHEATS, leaving HEATS; 'terrible' rearranges that into HASTE, which goes under MAKE.
explanation.definitionFit: 'Look sharp!' is an order to hurry up, the same as to make haste.

clue.text: Selection of swing-music is abruptly rejected as standard

indicators.note: something rejected is thrown back, so the picked letters are read backwards
a selection is a run of letters picked out from inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: Swing music is curtly dismissed as a run-of-the-mill choice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Selection of' takes CISAB from 'music is abruptly'; 'rejected' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: Basic means standard in the sense of plain, with no extras.

clue.text: I haven't got a clue!

parts.note: a crossword solver stuck on a clue would say they cannot work it out, which is the everyday exclamation of bafflement

explanation.surface: A cry of baffled ignorance, perhaps from a crossword solver.
explanation.walkthrough: The joke is that a solver could be saying it about the puzzle itself.
explanation.definitionFit: 'Beats me' is the colloquial way of saying you have no idea.

clue.text: Study session may see lots of fish encountered rising across river

parts.note: a large group of fish swimming together is a school

indicators.note: a piece set across another lies inside it, so one letter goes within the others
in a down answer something rising is read from bottom to top, so the word is reversed

parts.note: met means encountered

explanation.surface: A fishy scene of shoals meeting as they swim upstream over a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rising' turns MET into TEM; 'across' puts it round R to give TERM.
explanation.definitionFit: A school term is a period of study in the academic year.

clue.text: Had Clarets beaten two of these in Liverpool?

definitions.note: the definition stands for the plural word; Liverpool famously has two great cathedrals, Anglican and Catholic

indicators.note: something beaten is knocked out of shape, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A football question: did Burnley beat both Liverpool sides?
explanation.walkthrough: Clarets is the nickname of Burnley football club, and Liverpool has two clubs, Liverpool and Everton, which is the false trail. The city also has two cathedrals, one Anglican and one Catholic.
explanation.definitionFit: Liverpool is known for its pair of large twentieth-century cathedrals, so the answer names them.

clue.text: A charge for crossing island

parts.note: a toll is a charge paid to use a road or bridge

explanation.surface: A fee to pay for getting across to an island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for crossing' suggests a toll bridge but only links the pieces to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An atoll is a ring-shaped coral island.

clue.text: Very quickly becoming fond of spirits?

definitions.meaning: an idiom for doing something at once
taken literally, to ... is to enjoy a measure of whisky or other spirits

explanation.surface: Someone takes to drink with alarming speed.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means immediately and eagerly, while the literal reading is enjoying a dram of liquor.

clue.text: What one on fiddle must do to be clear about situation?

definitions.text: What one on fiddle must do
definitions.meaning: a violinist has to be familiar with the written music, the score
an idiom for understanding how things stand

explanation.surface: A violinist must master the music to grasp what is going on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fiddle' hints at cheating, where knowing the score would also fit, but here it is a violin.
explanation.definitionFit: Knowing the score literally means having learnt the music; idiomatically it means understanding the facts of the matter.

clue.text: Smarmy new goalie with talent …

indicators.note: a new version of a word is a fresh arrangement of its letters

parts.note: nous is practical intelligence or know-how, a talent

explanation.surface: A greasy new goalkeeper who has some talent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' rearranges GOALIE into OLEAGI, followed by NOUS. Nous is common sense, which is a looser fit for talent than it first seems.
explanation.definitionFit: Oleaginous literally means oily, and figuratively describes someone ingratiatingly smarmy.

clue.text: … and what he has on second report was fiddled!

indicators.note: something fiddled has been tampered with, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: The goalie's kit is mentioned, then a second report turns out to be rigged.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis carries on from the previous clue, so 'he' is the new goalie. 'fiddled' rearranges REPORT WAS into PORTSWEAR after S.
explanation.definitionFit: A goalkeeper on the pitch wears athletic clothing, so sportswear is what he has on.

clue.text: Catch sight of friend sent back for computers

indicators.note: something sent back is returned, so the letters are read backwards

parts.note: to spot is to catch sight of
a pal is a friend

explanation.surface: Seeing a friend returning some machines.
explanation.definitionFit: Laptops are portable computers small enough to sit on someone's lap.

clue.text: Dependant requiring a command to be in place

indicators.note: letters required to be in another word go inside it

parts.note: a site is a place
to tell someone to do something is to command them

explanation.surface: Someone reliant on others needs an order to stay put.
explanation.definitionFit: A satellite is a state or person under the control of a more powerful one, a dependant.

clue.text: Officer must cut complete protection

indicators.note: the officer cuts into the other word, so the letters go inside it

parts.note: sheer means complete or utter, as in sheer folly
LT is the abbreviation for lieutenant, an officer

explanation.surface: An officer is told to cut a full protective layer.
explanation.definitionFit: A shelter is a place or structure that gives protection from danger or weather.

clue.text: Foolish leader going off towards the rear

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter, and it goes away

parts.note: daft means foolish

explanation.surface: A silly leader heads off to the back.
explanation.definitionFit: Aft is the nautical term for at or towards the stern, the rear of a ship.

clue.text: A jar full of mainly creamy fruit

indicators.note: a pot full of something holds it inside, so letters go within it

parts.note: a pot is a jar

indicators.note: 'mainly' means most of the word, so its last letter is dropped

parts.note: rich food is creamy and heavy

explanation.surface: A jar packed with something creamy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mainly' drops the last letter of the creamy word, and 'full of' puts what is left inside the jar.
explanation.definitionFit: An apricot is a small orange stone fruit.

clue.text: Difficult to stifle answer in church parody …

indicators.note: the built letters are placed in the word for church, which wraps round them

parts.note: CE is the Church of England

indicators.note: something stifled is smothered from all sides, so a letter goes inside

parts.note: hard means difficult

explanation.surface: Holding back an answer in a mocking church service.
explanation.definitionFit: A charade is an absurd pretence, a mockery or travesty of the real thing.

clue.text: Doctor learnt about hospital transport

indicators.note: the jumbled letters go about the other letter, surrounding it
to doctor something is to tamper with it, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A doctor who has studied hospital transport.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctor' turns LEARNT into ENTRAL, which goes 'about' H. Transport here is the verb meaning to delight, not vehicles.
explanation.definitionFit: To transport someone is to carry them away with delight, just as to enthral does.

clue.text: … however tempting at first consideration

parts.note: though means however

indicators.note: 'at first' takes only the opening letter of the word before it

explanation.surface: Continuing from the previous clue: a tempting idea gets a second look.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis links the surface to the clue before; it plays no part in the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A thought is an idea or a piece of consideration given to something.

clue.text: I play for time during race for investiture

indicators.note: one thing happening during another sits within it, so letters go inside

parts.note: a nation is a people or race
to stall is to delay deliberately

explanation.surface: A runner stalls in the middle of a race.
explanation.walkthrough: 'race' looks like a contest but means a people.
explanation.definitionFit: An installation is the formal placing of someone in office, as an investiture is.

clue.text: Colour of metal for example given a lift

parts.note: tin is a metal

indicators.note: in a down answer something lifted is read upwards, so the letters are reversed

explanation.surface: The colour of a metal sample being hoisted up.
explanation.definitionFit: A tinge is a slight trace of colour.

clue.text: Company doctor's search

parts.note: MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is a doctor's qualification; the 's stands for 'is', linking to the definition

explanation.surface: A company doctor is investigating something.
explanation.definitionFit: To comb an area is to search it thoroughly, as if with a comb.

clue.text: Recess, beset by rising despair

indicators.note: in a down answer rising letters read from the bottom up, so they are reversed
the answer is surrounded by other letters of the word, so it lies inside

explanation.surface: A break in proceedings plagued by growing despair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beset by' finds ESPA in dESPAir; 'rising' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: An apse is a vaulted recess at the end of a church.

clue.text: Duck exercise and limit action

parts.note: a duck is a score of zero in cricket, the letter O
PE is physical education, exercise at school
to ration is to limit

explanation.surface: Instructions to dodge, train and cut back on activity.
explanation.definitionFit: An operation is an action or piece of activity, especially a planned one.

clue.text: Doctor must keep our strange band

indicators.note: something that keeps another holds it inside, so letters go within

parts.note: a GP is a general practitioner, a family doctor

indicators.note: something strange is out of its usual order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A doctor is told to put up with an odd musical band.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strange' jumbles the letters of our, and 'must keep' holds them inside the doctor.
explanation.definitionFit: A group is a band of musicians, or any band of people.

clue.text: Staff initially push for increase

indicators.note: 'initially' takes just the first letter of the word before it

parts.note: to urge is to push someone to act

explanation.surface: Employees begin by pressing for a pay rise.
explanation.definitionFit: A surge is a sudden increase, as in a surge in demand.

clue.text: The Spanish board will accept European Community is capable of winning votes

indicators.note: to accept something is to take it in, so letters go inside the others

parts.note: el is Spanish for 'the'
a table is a board, as in board and lodging

explanation.surface: A Spanish committee takes in Brussels and becomes a vote-winner.
explanation.definitionFit: An electable candidate is one with a realistic chance of being voted in.
